content:
maria: quick brainstorm: the last hedging canary looked fine latency-wise but cost blew up for certain route patterns. we need a safety model in the policy engine that prevents unbounded hedging. ideas?

alex: two orthogonal levers: 1) tokenized quota (spendable tokens per tenant/route) and 2) penalty ramping where each additional replica gets exponentially worse cost_score.

sam: token quota feels nice because it's predictable. we can top-up tokens per minute based on commitment tier. once tokens exhausted, hedging is denied. cheap to enforce at chooser.
jia: tokens are good but need to avoid cliff effects. suggest a sliding window refill and a "grace buffer" so one burst doesn't immediately kill latency. also expose a metric for tokens_left_by_route.
devon: enforcement detail: do we rely on chooser sidecar hinting or centralized admission? my vote: chooser enforces local cap; central policy server decides quotas and can push emergency reductions.
lena: thought: shadow-hedging mode for new rules where we simulate hedging behavior without actually launching replicas; collect cost_projection_per_route and impact_on-tail. helps us tune budgets before enabling.
alex: love shadow mode. runtime change: policy compiler should emit a static upper_bound for hedging that runtime uses as a safety limit.
maria: small DSL sketch for quota+ramp:
```
policy {
  target: route
  hedging {
    base_replica: 1
    max_replica: 3
    quota_tokens_per_minute: 60
    ramp: [1.0, 2.0, 4.0] # multiplicative cost weight per replica
    grace_tokens: 5
    shadow: true
  }
  fallback: model-compact
}
```

sam: note: ramp values map to cost_score adjustments used in resolver scoring. need to make sure we also surface cost_delta annotation in traces so billing/ops can attribute charges.
jia: telemetry additions: tokens_consumed_rate, projected_cost_if_unbounded, shadow_deltas_hist, and hedged_success_rate. alert if projected_cost_if_unbounded > budget_threshold for 10m.
devon: rollout plan: 1) implement tokens in policy store + chooser check (no hard cap), 2) enable shadow mode for affected routes, 3) flip to enforce with grace buffer, 4) monitor for SLO regressions. ops-bot: note: rollout should include canary tag and the deploy bot will annotate traffic.
lena: edge case: model variants with very different per-token cost. quota should be normalized by variant_cost_factor. otherwise tenant gaming possible.
alex: good call. add variant_cost_factor into policy compile output. runtime must multiply token cost by that factor.
maria: operational playbook idea: if we see a sudden spike in tokens_consumed_rate, short-term mitigation: 1) reduce per-minute quota by 50% for offending tenant, 2) force fallback to model-compact, 3) notify SLA owners. keep steps automated where possible.
sam: question: do we allow route owners to self-serve higher quotas via console? would be nice but needs approval flow for billing. maybe console requests create approval ticket with auto-escalation.
jia: console flow ok as long as default is conservative. also add a test harness: synthetic workload generator that can exercise hedging policies in dev and staging.
devon: implementation note: chooser will cache token_state for 1s to avoid hot-path RPCs; central store syncs per 5s. that's acceptable given granularity. we should document eventual consistency caveats.
lena: regression test ideas: 1) ensure tokens are not double-spent across replicas, 2) variant_cost normalization correctness, 3) shadow mode metrics match actual when enabled.
maria: action items: @alex add variant_cost metadata to model catalog and make policy compiler emit normalization, @jia add the telemetry metrics and alerts, @devon implement token store prototype and chooser integration, @sam make canary dashboard and synthetic workload config, @lena write regression unit tests and shadow-mode harness. i'll write a short RFC summary and link to this thread.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: "canary-tag added: hedge-safety-v1; scheduled rollout windows set" :rocket

alex: i'll start a small branch for catalog changes and compile output.
sam: i'll draft the dashboard tiles and an initial alert runbook.
jia: will prototype metrics and a Prometheus exporter for tokens.
maria: thanks team   let's reconvene Fri 9am to review first shadow metrics. :+1:
